newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar eases visa rules to attract Gulf tourists.
newsitem.headline: Qatar eases visa rules to attract Gulf tourists.

text.p: Qatar has introduced new visa rules allowing entry without a prior permit to expatriate professionals in other Gulf Arab states as part of plans to develop tourism in the small desert state, officials said.

"Visit visas for GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) residents will be issued at Doha International Airport or any other port of entry or border post," said Lieutenant-Colonel Jassim Mohamed al-Kuwari, director general of immigration on Thursday.

The rule, which came into force on Tuesday, applies only to expatriate professionals resident in the other GCC states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain and United Arab Emirates -- came into effect on Tuesday.
"The relaxation in the rule is aimed at revitalising the market economy -- especially the souk economy -- and tourism," said an official at the government's tourism department.

Qatar, with a native population of 160,000 and total population including expatriates of 650,000, has recently begun promoting tourism and refurbishing beach resorts. "Last year, around 900,000 people visited Qatar. We plan to lift this to 1.2 million this year and two million by 2000," he said.
